title: A regularization method for quantum neural networks using data symmetry
abstract: Leveraging data symmetries has recently become a key strategy in quantum neural networks (QNNs) to improve generalization and training efficiency. In this study, we propose a novel regularization method for QNNs based on input data symmetry. By introducing a penalty term that encourages the model to align with data symmetry, our method enables improved training speed and generalization. This symmetry-based regularization is simple to implement and does not require prior knowledge of the symmetry group. We validate its effectiveness through numerical experiments on both classification tasks and quantum generative adversarial networks. Empirical results demonstrate faster convergence and lower test errors. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical generalization bound using Rademacher complexity and conjecture a condition under which models with symmetry exhibit better generalization. Our findings highlight the potential of symmetry-aware regularization in enhancing the performance of QML models.
summary: This paper introduces a regularization technique for Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) that leverages inherent data symmetries to enhance training efficiency and generalization. By adding a penalty term based on symmetry constraints, the method improves performance in both classification and generative tasks. The work combines empirical validation with theoretical bounds derived from Rademacher complexity.
main_problem: The study aims to improve the generalization performance and accelerate training of Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) by incorporating constraints derived from input data symmetries.
main_result: The proposed symmetry-based regularization method leads to faster convergence and lower test errors across both classification and quantum generative adversarial network tasks. Theoretically, it provides a bound suggesting improved generalization when the model respects data symmetry.
method: A novel penalty term, $C_{	ext{symm}}$, is added to the cost function, penalizing deviations between the parameterized unitary circuit and the unitary derived from the input data symmetry. Theoretical analysis uses Rademacher complexity bounds to quantify generalization improvements.
model_or_system: The model consists of QNNs implemented via parameterized quantum circuits $U(	heta)$, whose output is measured by an expectation value $\langle\psi(x, 	heta)| O |\psi(x, 	heta)angle$. The input data symmetry is characterized by the commutation relation $[ho_{	ext{in}}(x), S] = 0$.
key_observables: Test errors (classification), FID scores (generative tasks), penalty loss ($C_{	ext{symm}}$), and Rademacher complexity ($\mathcal{R}_{\Theta}(F)$).
important_parameters: The balancing parameter $C$ controlling the regularization strength, and the choice of matrix norm used in theoretical bounds.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that enforcing data symmetry acts as a beneficial inductive bias. A limitation noted is that excessive symmetries can overly restrict expressibility.
figures_summary: Figures show loss curves for classification tasks comparing $C=0$ vs. $C>0$, and FID scores for generative tasks, illustrating the impact of the regularization strength on training stability and performance.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the symmetry-based regularization method ($C_{	ext{symm}}$), validates it empirically across classification and QGAN tasks using various circuit types (AA, CB), and supports these findings with theoretical generalization bounds derived from Rademacher complexity.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the intersection of quantum computation and machine learning theory by providing a principled way to regularize variational quantum circuits using underlying physical symmetries, which is relevant for designing robust quantum algorithms.
